News.title: Moment Starmer caught in Commons bust-up with Speaker as PM given dressing down over dodging Kemi’s
News.content:
THIS is the moment Sir Keir Starmer has a testy bust-up with the Commons Speaker after getting a dressing-down over dodging questions.

He is seen confronting Sir Lindsay Hoyle at the end of PMQs today, where he had been admonished for veering off topic.





At one point the Prime Minister can be seen hitting his fist against the side of the Speaker’s chair.

Tonight the Speaker confirmed that he has raised the problem repeatedly with No10 staff in private.

It comes amid Tory fury that the PM has been dodging Kemi Badenoch‘s questions in recent weeks.

Sir Lindsay Hoyle was forced to admonish the PM in the chamber today after repeatedly pivoting off points put to him by Kemi Badenoch.

He blasted: “Prime Minister, it is Prime Minister’s questions. We have got to concentrate.”

Tonight the Speaker’s office appeared to confirm their exchange at the end of the session surrounded the PM’s question-dodging.

A spokeswoman for the Speaker said that “answers should be confined to the points contained in the question.



“Every so often the Speaker has to remind Prime Ministers – and Ministers – of the rules of engagement in the Chamber.

“The Speaker has made this point to officials at No 10 on several occasions recently as well.”

In recent weeks Tory MPs have been furiously gesturing at the Speaker to insist he intervenes in Sir Keir’s potentially evasive answers.

The PM has repeatedly used questions on the Iran crisis to attack Ms Badenoch for initially wanting to support the American strikes.

Today he also accused her of the “mother of all u-turns” after being asked about when his Defence Investment Plan will be published.



Sir Lindsay’s spokeswoman said: “The Speaker is not responsible for the questions asked by Members or the answers given by Ministers.

“Questions to Ministers should relate to matters for which they are officially responsible.”

It is the third occasion that the Prime Minister has been reprimanded for not answering questions.



Last month, the Speaker said during PMQs: “I am sorry I am interrupting you, but unfortunately we have to stick to Prime Minister’s questions, not Leader of the Opposition’s questions.”

He picked Sir Keir up on the same point in January and said: “We do not ask the Opposition questions. These are questions for the Prime Minister, not the other way around.”

This comes as Sir Keir faces mounting pressure to reveal Labour’s defence investment plan for the next decade.

Today the PM avoided answering on when the vital plan might appear and ignored one question on a ship-upgrade plan.

Ms Badenoch used recent accusations from George Robertson as ammunition. The ex-Labour Defence Sec and former NATO chief slammed Sir Keir for delaying on defence funding and not providing key investment.



Lord Robertson said the government had left UK security in “peril” in a speech yesterday.

The PM disagreed with the claims and said the Labour party had committed to “the biggest boost to defence spending since the Cold War”.

Ms Badenoch retorted: “talking about an increase is not the same as giving an increase”.

She later referenced the Westminster summer of sex campaign in which Labour MP Samantha Niblett said she would bring sex toys into parliament in the hopes of improving education.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Tory leader told the Commons: “This is a moment of profound national seriousness. And what are they doing?



“They are promoting sex toys in parliament. That’s what they’re doing. It gives a while new meaning to fiddling while Rome burns.”

News.title: SantaCon founder on naughty list after ‘stealing’ over $1m meant for charities from his Christmas-themed bar crawl
News.content:
THE founder of SantaCon is on the naughty list after staying true to the New York City charity’s name, authorities have claimed.

Stefan Pildes has been dubbed a “Scrooge” after donating just a small fraction of the nearly $3 million he raised through festive bar crawls, according to an indictment.





His SantaCon charity fundraisers floods New York City with thousands of drunk young people in red and white Santa costumes every holiday season.

But, he has been splashing much of the donated cash on property renovations, concerts and posh holidays, alleged federal authorities.

“Instead of donating the millions of dollars he raised, he ran his own con game,” US Attorney Jay Clayton claimed in a news release today.

“He took advantage of New Yorkers’ generous holiday spirit to finance his lifestyle through personal expenses, big and small. No matter how you dress it up, fraud is fraud.”

Pildes allegedly “pocketed over half of the proceeds generated by his nonprofit to make personal purchases,” said FBI assistant director in charge, James C. Barnacle, Jr.

Barnacle slammed Pildes, 50, of Hewitt, New Jersey, as a “Scrooge” who ripped off kind-hearted New Yorkers.

The suspected fraudster, who was arrested today, allegedly stole Christmas donations from tens of thousands of victims and deprived local charities of more than $1 million, Barnacle added.

Authorities said he siphoned more than half of the proceeds raised each year to an entity he controlled.



Pildes was president and controlled Participatory Safety Inc., the nonprofit entity that organized SantaCon, they added.

According to the indictment, he had been splashing much of the donated funds on himself over the past five years.

This was despite Pildes claiming he received no compensation from the popular festive event.

Donations were allegedly used to finance his personal needs, including renovations to a lakefront property in New Jersey, and concert tickets.



He also allegedly splurged on luxury vacations in Hawaii and Las Vegas, extravagant meals and a luxury vehicle, said court filings.

About $2.7 million was raised through SantaCon charity events from 2019 to 2024.

The SantaCon website describes the event as a charitable, non-political, nonsensical Santa Claus convention, according to the indictment.

The tradition features a ticketed bar crawl through city streets each December that has attracted over 25,000 people dressed as holiday-themed characters.

Pildes solicited bars and restaurants to participate and donate from 10% to 25% of their food and beverage sales to his charity organization, according to the indictment.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“When individuals exploit charitable causes for personal gain, they undermine the trust our communities place in organizations meant to serve the public good,” said IRS-CI special agent in charge, Jennifer L. Piovesan.

An indictment unsealed today at Manhattan federal court – where he’s due to make an initial appearance before a magistrate judge – has charged him with wire fraud.

News.title: Five convicted ‘from Latin gang’ for stabbing man, 21, to death in London over feud after chasing victim down alleyway
News.content:
STREET WAR Five convicted ‘from Latin gang’ for stabbing man, 21, to death in London over feud after chasing victim down alleyway

FIVE men from the ‘Latin Gang’ have been found guilty of murder after a tense 11-week trial at the Old Bailey.

Giovanny Rendon Bedoya was brutally stabbed and killed in south London after a violent confrontation between two groups.





The 21-year-old was chased through the streets of Walworth before being cornered and attacked in April 2025.

The court heard how Giovanny was pursued down an alleyway near Hillingdon Street and Langdale Close, SE17, before being set upon by the group.

Cops were called at 9.16pm on April 14 last year to reports of men fighting with knives in the area.

Officers found Giovanny behind residential flats on Hillingdon Street suffering from multiple stab wounds.

Despite desperate efforts by emergency services, he was pronounced dead at 10.07pm.

A post-mortem later confirmed he died from multiple sharp-force injuries.

Detectives said the attack came amid rising tensions between two groups.



A jury returned unanimous guilty verdicts on Tuesday, April 14, following a detailed investigation by the Met Police.

Joseph Jimenez, 22, of no fixed address, Angel Gonzalez Angulo, 19, of Camberwell Church Street, Bryan Villada Hernandez, 20, of Langdale Close, Zozoro Mohamed Olivier Boizo, 21, of Lorrimore Square, and Christian Batista Gonzalez, 22, of Moyers Road were all convicted of murder.

The court heard Hernandez was arrested at the scene shortly after the attack.



Forensic tests later found the victim’s blood on his tracksuit, along with damage consistent with contact from a knife.

Messages recovered from his phone showed discussions about destroying evidence and concerns about police activity.

Cops trawled through more than 1,500 hours of CCTV footage during the investigation.

Footage revealed a nearby address on Langdale Close was being used as a squat.

After the killing, Angulo and Boizo fled the address and travelled by taxi to a friend’s home.



CCTV later captured Angulo changing clothes and carrying a bin bag, which prosecutors said was used to dispose of blood-stained items and weapons.

Gonzalez fled the UK following the attack and was arrested near Barcelona on May 19, 2025.

He was later extradited back to the UK to face justice.

Jimenez was arrested in Chichester after fleeing London.

Detective Chief Inspector Kate Blackburn, who led the investigation, said: “This was a sustained and extremely violent attack, carried out by a group acting together.



“Giovanny was chased and killed in brutal circumstances, and today’s convictions reflect the strength of the evidence and the determination of the investigation team.

“Our thoughts remain with Giovanny’s family and loved ones, who have shown immense dignity throughout these proceedings.

“Such brutality has no place on our streets – it rips families and communities apart.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“That’s why the Met is doing everything it can to target dangerous offenders and prevent senseless violence.”

All five men are due to be sentenced at the Old Bailey on Wednesday, May 20.

News.title: Idiot YouTuber Johnny Somali is JAILED after kissing WW2 sex slave statue in attention-seeking stunt
News.content:
KISS GOODBYE Idiot YouTuber Johnny Somali is JAILED after kissing WW2 sex slave statue in attention-seeking stunt

A YOUTUBER has been jailed in South Korea over a shocking stunt at a WWII sex slave memorial.

Johnny Somali – real name Ramsey Khalid – sparked outrage after filming himself kissing and performing lap dances on a statue dedicated to victims of sexual abuse during the Second World War.





An estimated 200,000 women across Asia were forced into sexual slavery by Japanese soldiers during the conflict.

Many were Korean, while others came from China, the Philippines, Indonesia and Taiwan.

The statues, which often depict a young woman seated in a chair, were installed by activists to honour and remember these women.



They remain a deeply sensitive symbol, particularly in South Korea.

Authorities in Seoul charged Khalid with public nuisance in November 2024 after he shared footage of the stunt online.

He has been barred from leaving the country ever since.

On Wednesday, a court convicted the 25-year-old on multiple counts, sentencing him to six months in prison.



“The defendant repeatedly committed crimes against unspecified members of the public to generate profit via YouTube and distributed the content in disregard of Korean law,” the court said.

Prosecutors had initially pushed for a three-year sentence, but the judge opted for a lesser penalty.

According to the Korea Herald, the court cited an “absence of severe harm to victims.”

Khalid will also face restrictions after his release, including a ban on working with organisations that serve minors and people with disabilities.

He apologised back in 2024, saying he “didn’t understand the significance of the statute”.



The YouTuber, who has around 5,000 subscribers, has built a reputation for provocative and controversial content.

This has lead to him being banned on multiple streaming platforms.

During the investigation, Khalid continued to attract criticism.

He posted videos challenging locals to fight him, causing disturbances on public transport, and vandalising a convenience store.

His history of controversy extends beyond South Korea.



In 2024, he was detained at a protest in Tel Aviv after making inappropriate remarks to a female police officer, though he was later released.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A year earlier in Japan, he drew widespread backlash after taunting locals about the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki during the final days of the war.

He was later fined £1,030 for disrupting a restaurant by playing loud music.

News.title: Huge blaze erupts at oil refinery with smoke & fire seen from miles as residents told stay away & keep windows shut
News.content:
A MASSIVE fire has broken out at a major oil refinery as locals are warned to stay indoors.

A huge blaze and billowing black smoke can be seen for miles as firefighters try to control the blaze.





Multiple explosions could be heard coming from the Geelong Refinery, an hour south west of Melbourne, Australia, around 11pm local time (2pm BST) on Wednesday.

At least 10 emergency vehicles are currently at the scene tackling the “significant” blaze which is not yet under control.

The Country Fire Authority issued a watch and act for a large swathe of Geelong urging locals to take shelter indoors immediately.

“There is a factory fire in Refinery Road, Corio,” the advice said.

“A wind change has caused the smoke to be blown towards the Northern Geelong area.”

Residents were also being urged to keep off the roads to allow emergency services to respond.



The site is one of only two operational oil refineries in the country.

It supplies more than 50 per cent of Victoria’s fuel and around 10 per cent of Australia‘s fuel.

It can process up to 120,00 barrels of oil a day, including “manufacturing petrol, diesel, LPG, jet fuel, avgas and Low Aromatic Fuel”.

It’s understood more than 1,100 people work at the site.

On Monday the US announced it would blockade Iranian ports after the mullahs closed the Strait of Hormuz to most shipping.



Oil has soared to over $100 a barrel and prices at the fuel pump have rocketed across the world.

It comes as confusion reigns in the crucial waterway, where several Iranian-linked ships appeared to defy Trump’s blockade.

Four ships seemed to sail through undeterred by the American threats, but at least one appeared to do a U-turn soon after exiting the strait.

The US said six ships complied with orders to turn back.

Trump told the New York Post on Tuesday that talks between the US and Iran could restart “over next two days” in Islamabad.



The US president first said discussions about more talks were “happening, but, you know, a little bit slow”, before adding that “something could be happening over the next two days” in the Pakistani capital.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Direct talks between the US and Iran ended without a deal on Saturday – JD Vance said that the sticking point was uranium enrichment.

News.title: Glasgow tourist, 26, fighting for life after horror scooter crash in Bali as family issue desperate plea
News.content:
FAMILY'S HEARTACHE Glasgow tourist, 26, fighting for life after horror scooter crash in Bali as family issue desperate plea

A GLASGOW traveller is fighting for his life after a horror scooter crash in Bali.

The terrifying smash left Euan Kay with two bleeds on the brain, dislodged broken bones and serious facial injuries.





The 26-year-old’s family is now desperately trying to raise funds in a bid to secure life-saving surgery for Euan.

Euan stopped off in Bali for a holiday before heading back to Glasgow after a year in Australia.

His loved ones received a devastating call at around midnight today following the serious crash on the Indonesian island.

Euan, who was wearing a helmet at the time, fell off a scooter during a torrential downpour.



His family have been told he has a 30 to 70 per cent chance of survival due to his injuries if he does not get surgery.

His sister Fiona says they have been left “absolutely distraught”.

The gofundme page read: “We got the worst phone call a family could receive late last night that Euan, our youngest brother, has been in a serious scooter accident in Bali.

“Euan has two bleeds in the brain and the neurosurgeon is needing to operate today.



“He also has numerous broken bones that have snapped and dislodged and is also requiring major surgery for and life changing facial injuries.

“We have been given 30-70 per cent chance of survival for his injuries if he does not get surgery. We are absolutely distraught.”

And unfortunately, Euan’s travel insurance does not cover such accidents.

They are now frantically trying to fundraise enough money for the surgery after they were told by medics that it would cost around £20,000 to operate.

Euan’s mum is also looking to fly out to be with her son.



Over £32,000 has already been raised in around eight hours since it was launched.

The appeal added: “Unfortunately Euan does not have insurance for this type of accident and we have had the hospital on the phone needing £20,000 before they will operate.

“He is needing life-saving surgery today and we need to get my mum over there too.

“Any help would be appreciated at this very distressing time for us all. Please keep Euan in your prayers.



“I know how loved Euan is all over the world and everyone that knows him knows he lives life to the full.

“He was on route home to Glasgow after an amazing year in Australia.

“He stopped off in Bali for a holiday before heading back to Glasgow.

“We just want him home asap but it’s going to be a long road ahead of him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You can do this Euan we will be with you as soon as possible. We love you.”



You can donate to the fundraiser here.

News.title: Chilling new details emerge after home invader seen in terrifying viral doorbell video makes first court appearance
News.content:
CHILLING new details have emerged about a home invader who terrorised a mum and daughter in a viral doorbell video.

Jason Thomas Nichols, 30, is accused of breaking into a California home after threatening to kill a pregnant mum and her son, 5, inside.





In the shocking footage, the man tries to kick down the front door of a Bay area home while screaming to be let inside.

Making his first appearance in court on Wednesday, Nichols wore a striped jail jumpsuit and was shackled at the waist.

He reportedly smiled and rolled his eyes through some of the proceedings while also thanking reporters for taking his photo.

Nichols was charged with four felonies, including burglary, assault with a deadly weapon, vandalism and making criminal threats.

A brave witness also came forward with new allegations about an encounter with Nichols and a child two days before the home invasion.

Nichols now faces a fifth charge of annoying or molesting a child under 18.

The footage of a creep breaking into the Fairfield home went viral online earlier this week.



The conversation begins innocently, as a man in a long black coat, flip flops and glasses asks the owner to “please” open the door.

The man, later identified by authorities as Jason Nichols, 30, explains: “I just want to make sure everything is OK. I just figured I would check on something.”

A woman with her child are inside the house at the time but she is too terrified to open the door.

Her husband, who isn’t at home, tries to persuade Nichols to go away via the doorcam microphone.

The owner replies: “I don’t know what you want man, get out of my house.”



That reply infuriates Nichols, who kicked the front door and started screaming in fury.

“Open this f***ing door. Where is your daughter man? Who’s in there with you. Open the door or I’m breaking it f***ing down. Is everybody in this house OK?” he rages.

The homeowner can be heard begging him to leave.



Nichols then asks in a menacing tone: “Open the door. This is my neighbourhood. Now…. Or I’ll f***ing end you. Do you understand me?”

He then aggressively rips off the doorbell while pounding the door.

During the ordeal, Nichols identifies himself as Harry Dresden from the popular Jim Butcher Dresden File novels about a private investigator/wizard.

Nichols then reportedly found a way inside the home by slipping through a sliding glass door.

Another security camera inside the house caught Nichols striding through the house, opening cupboards and doors looking for the wife and child.



The homeowner raced back to his home armed with a shovel to protect his wife and child.

He and Nichols reportedly exchanged blows causing each other head injuries, police said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fairfield police arrived just minutes later and found Nichols outside.

He was taken to a nearby hospital before being booked into jail on multiple felony charges tied to the brazen break-in attempt.

News.title: Iran using ceasefire to DIG OUT buried missile launchers, satellite pics show – as regime threatens to shut the Red Sea
News.content:
IRAN is using the temporary ceasefire to dig out missile launchers that were buried by US-Israeli blitzes of the rogue nation earlier in the war.

Shocking satellite photos reveal the ruthless regime will not rest during the pause in bombing and is instead using the truce to clear the way to its underground missile bases.





It comes as Iran threatens to unleash its Houthi proxy to block a second critical chokepoint for global trade – the Bab al-Mandab Strait, also known as the Gate of Tears.

The Gate of Tears is a crucial global shipping artery leading to the Suez Canal – around 10 per cent of all global trade passes through the strait at the mouth of the Red Sea.

The bases were strategically targeted by US and Israeli blitzes that blocked their entrances and exits.



It was part of a plan to trap Iran‘s missile launchers underground.

By blocking the ways in and out of the bases, targeted strikes intended to stop launchers from firing or re-loading.

But now the rogue nation is using the time allotted for peace talks to clear debris from the bases.

Satellite pictures show rubble being scooped up and loaded onto trucks to unblock entrances at bases in Tabriz and Khomeyn.



And US intelligence estimates suggest that around half of Tehran’s missile launchers are still intact.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said this week that operation Epic Fury had “functionally destroyed” Iran’s missile program, leaving the rogue nation “combat ineffective for years to come.”

But US officials told the Wall Street Journal that Iran may well be able to dig out and repair many of its buried missile launchers.

It comes as the US is piling more troops into the region after imposing a blockade on ships visiting Iranian ports in the Gulf.

The US is enforcing a blockade on Iranian-linked ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.



Although some ships seemed to have slipped through in the first 24 hours, the Americans insisted the vessels then complied with orders to stop or turn around.

The US blockade is a response to the Iranians refusing to reopen the Strait – free passage through the waterway was a key condition for the two-week ceasefire.

Trump has declared that the Iran war is “close to over” – hinting at talks in the next two days.

He was picked up on constantly referring to the war in the past tense in a Tuesday evening interview with Fox News.



When asked if he believed the war was really over, Trump replied: “I think it’s close to over. I view it as very close to over.”

The president doubled down by telling Sky News that a deal with Iran is “very possible” ahead of King Charles‘ state visit to the US later this month.

Israel expects the two-week ceasefire agreed last Tuesday to be extended.



But Trump reportedly told ABC News that he thought a deal would be agreed without an extension, saying: “I think you’re going to be watching an amazing two days ahead.”

Iran refused to relinquish its nuclear ambitions at last week’s crunch peace talks in Pakistan, but JD Vance is now prepared to tighten the screws for round two.

Vance said his boss was determined to remove Iran’s nuclear threat by stopping all Uranium enrichment, insisting Trump wants a “grand bargain” – not a “small deal”

If they continue to block peace, Trump’s next move may be a potentially catastrophic ground offensive by the 10,000-strong US invasion force he has shipped to the region.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Around 6,000 soldiers aboard the USS George H W Bush aircraft carrier and its escort ships are heading to the Middle East.



More than 3,000 crack airborne troops have already been sent to join 5,000 US Marines closing in on Iran.

News.title: 'Tech giants must face tough consequences for spouting harmful content'
News.content:
'Tech giants must face tough consequences for spouting harmful content'

Tech firms, such as Meta, TikTok and Google, tend to dodge real accountability despite harming children with content designed to hook young people — and this has to stop

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

The Government must tackle tech firms

Bereaved parents are right to be angry because while children are being harmed, Big Tech carries on largely unchecked. The likes of Meta, TikTok and Google have built platforms designed to hook young users, yet too often dodge real accountability. Keir Starmer is right that “looking the other way is not an option.” But meetings, consultations and warm words are no substitute for action. Parents who have lost children are demanding change, and they deserve more than promises. For too long, tech firms have been allowed to police themselves, offering reassurances while harmful content, dangerous trends and addictive design continue to spread. That must end. If companies fail to get their house in order, there must be real consequences - heavy fines, tough sanctions and rules that are actually enforced. This is about more than regulation. It is about responsibility. Children’s safety cannot be left to corporate goodwill. If Big Tech won’t act, the Government must - and it must do so now.

‌



Amanda Knox's move is deeply insensitive

Amanda Knox’s planned UK visit risks reopening wounds that have never fully healed. Inviting Brits to “come say hello” just miles from where Meredith Kercher lived feels, at best, deeply insensitive. Knox, twice convicted and twice acquitted over the murder, has every right to rebuild her life. But turning that story into a career, through books, podcasts, stand-up and film, raises difficult questions. Her latest documentary, Mouth of the Wolf, revisits the scene of Meredith’s murder. For some, that’s compelling storytelling. For others, it reopens a tragedy that a grieving family have spent years trying to process. Supporters say Knox was wronged. Critics say she has monetised a brutal crime. Both may be true. But one fact remains: a young British woman lost her life, and her family still deserves peace.

John Virgo is greatly missed

A true national treasure, John Virgo brought joy, flair and unforgettable commentary to millions. As World Championship snooker returns to Sheffield, his absence will be deeply felt. The game has lost not just a voice, but a showman whose warmth and wit made the green baize part of Britain’s fabric.

News.title: MPs reject social media ban for under 16s as bereaved families issue warning
News.content:
MPs reject social media ban for under 16s as bereaved families issue warning

Bereaved parents have piled pressure on Keir Starmer to take urgent action on social media - as MPs voted down a proposal to ban under 16s from accessing platforms

View 2 Images Bereaved families handed in a letter to No10 calling for urgent action on social media

Bereaved parents have piled pressure on Keir Starmer to take urgent action on social media - as MPs voted down a proposal to ban under 16s from accessing platforms.

‌



Grieving parents whose children’s deaths are linked to social media criticised the Government’s lack of "decisive" action and warned it “risks being outmanoeuvred by the relentless pace of Big Tech”.

‌



Pressure is increasing on the PM to ban social media for under 16s, with peers this evening forcing a second vote on the issue in the Commons within six weeks.

‌



MPs rejected the latest amendment to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill, with MPs voting 256 to 150.

Last month, MPs voted 307 to 173 against the Lords proposal for an outright ban. One Labour MP John McDonnell previously rebelled against the Government to support a ban.

TikTok boss confronted over teen's unexplained death and missing data READ MORE :

View 2 Images The PM is under pressure to take action urgently (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

‌



The Government has not supported the amendments as it is currently consulting on a range of online safety measures, including a social media ban, as well as curbing addictive features on apps or introducing overnight curfews on sites.

Ahead of the vote, Education minister Olivia Bailey branded the Lords’ amendment “narrow”, telling MPs: “Our consultation allows us to address a much wider range of services and features. It also allows us to consider the different views about the way forward, and that's why it's crucial that we do not preempt the government's consultation, which will close next month.”

She also vowed there will not be “endless rounds of consultation,” telling the Commons: “The government will act. We have listened to the concerns raised in both houses regarding a desire for swift action and more specific power, and for appropriate scrutiny.”

‌



The minister added that the Government has tabled an amendment in place of the Lords’ demands which commits the Education Secretary to report to Parliament on progress in this area within six months of the bill becoming law.”

Ellen Roome, who believes her son Julian “Jools” Sweeney, 14, may have died doing an online challenge, was among bereaved parents who handed in a letter to No10 on Wednesday calling for urgent action. She was joined by the parents of Isaac Kenevan, Mia Janin, Noah Gibson and Maia Walsh.

“While other nations take decisive legislative action to protect their citizens, the UK remains in a cycle of consultation that risks being outmanoeuvred by the relentless pace of Big Tech,” they wrote.

‌



“We can no longer treat social media as a neutral tool; for children, it has become a form of ‘Digital Nicotine,’ engineered to bypass developmental safeguards and leading to profound, documented harms.

“There is now an overwhelming parliamentary and public consensus for change, evidenced by the decisive amendments recently passed in the House of Lords.”

Australia restricted access for under 16s at the end of last year, while other European countries including Spain and Greece have similar plans.

‌



Ms Roome’s campaign is supported by Lauren Cowell, Simon Cowell’s partner, who earlier this week spoke to The Mirror about her urgent demands. Ms Cowell confronted deputy Labour leader Lucy Powell on LBC radio, asking her why the Government had told Labour MPs to vote against the social media amendment. She told the senior MP: “As a mum myself, I want to ask why, when we all know the dangers of social media, the Labour government is whipping its own MPs to vote against measures that would protect children and young people right now?"

Ms Powell, who is a mum to teenagers, said she is in “two minds” about personally supporting a ban but said the government will bring in effective action “as quickly as possible”.

It comes as research by Opinium shows more than seven in 10 (72%) British parents want under-16s to be prevented from having social media accounts.

‌



Not all bereaved parents and online safety charities are supportive of a ban. Ian Russell, whose 14-year-old Molly Russell took her own life in 2017 due to online harms, among those who urge caution before rushing into a ban.

Andy Burrows, the CEO of the Molly Rose Foundation, named after Molly, said: “MPs have once again rejected the notion that we either have an Australia style-ban or stick with the completely unacceptable status quo with children continuing to come to preventable harm on social media.

“Our recent polling shows a majority of children are still accessing prohibited platforms in Australia with most not feeling safer or noticing improvements in their lives. It’s time to look beyond this false sense of safety and for the Prime Minister to decisively commit to strengthening regulation to make unsafe and addictive design a thing of the past.”

Article continues below

The charity has also pointed towards research which shows three in five (61%) Australian 12 to 15 year-olds still have access to one or more accounts despite a social media ban coming into force in the country at the end of last year.

News.title: Donald Trump thrashes out Iran deal - but it could 'rebound very poorly'
News.content:
Donald Trump thrashes out Iran deal - but it could 'rebound very poorly'

As the Strait of Hormuz crisis deepens Washington is facing politically damaging decision to agree to an Iran nuke deal that trump will feel is too close to the Obama deal he tore up in the first place

View 5 Images USS Marines aboard USS Tripoli practise for war (Image: US Central Command)

Washington is hoping Iran will agree to stall nuclear development for ten to 15 years in peace talks - but this would look similar to the nuke deal struck by President Obama.

‌



An ‘unsettled’ White House is thrashing out the possibility that even such a nuclear agreement to end the Iran war would mean an obvious climb-down to America’s original position.

‌



And US President Donald Trump, according to a senior Middle East expert, may not to agree as that would be damaging even beyond the political nightmare the war has already caused. The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action - JCPOA - AKA “the Iran Deal” was an agreement to limit the Iranian nuclear programme that was torn up by Trump. And further leverage is likely to be imposed by Iran on the US in terms of using the Yemeni Houthis to apply pressure on the Baba al-Mandeb passage, which is now being used.

‌



Fears grow that UK families could be impacted by summer holiday cancellations READ MORE :

View 5 Images Tension- US President Trump and UK's Keir Starmer (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Former CIA and State Department consultant Dr Ilan Bergman, senior Vice President at the American Foreign Policy Council told the Daily Mirror: “The shifting political messaging that's coming out of the White House from President Trump has been very variable.. Back in January, when you saw that revolt in Iran in which the regime responded by killing something like 36,000 opposition protesters, you heard from the White House that America was there and help was on the way.

“America was going to help Iranians liberate their country. We are long past that conversation. In fact, the President is doubling down on the idea that regime change has already occurred, which terribly, it has not because the system is still intact. Where the political conversation is right now is whether or not the current Iran leadership is prepared to do a deal with regard to we are not even now, at this point, talking about a permanent cessation of Iran's uranium enrichment.

‌



View 5 Images Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“The administration is increasingly talking about a time delay of something like 20 years and the Iranians have countered with five years. I think we know that where they're going to settle is somewhere between ten and 15 years, and also a rollback of Iran's ballistic missile arsenal and Iran's proxy network.

“The political problem that you have is the fact that, first of all, this sort of settlement looks an awful lot like the 2015 nuclear deal hammered out by President Obama, which President Trump, in his first term, abrogated because he said it was the worst deal ever. So it creates political problems for him, and also because we are pretty close chronologically to the US midterm elections. If the president hammers out a deal in which America looks like a loser, I think it rebounds very poorly for him at the ballot box.”

‌



View 5 Images Iranians burn US-Israeli flags in Tehran (Image: ABEDIN TAHERKENAREH/EPA/Shutterstock)

Currently the key oil trade waterway the Strait of Hormuz is blocked by Iran and blockaded by the United States Navy, which is turning Iran’s shipping back. Latest talks on a peace deal have fallen through and the April 8 two week ceasefire ends on April 22 with the possibility hostilities will start again.

There are also increasing fears Iran’s proxy force the Houthis in Yemen could become involved and help further block shipping with attempts to do so on the Baba al-Mandeb straight. This is a strategic link between the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea via the Red Sea and the Suez Canal. Most exports of petroleum and natural gas from the Persian Gulf that transit the Suez Canal or the SUMED Pipeline pass through both the Bab el-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz.

Article continues below

View 5 Images Close quarter training Marines on USS Tripoli (Image: US Central Command)

Dr Ilan added: “The Saudis activated the East West pipeline, which is a pipeline that runs across Saudi territory and dumps out into the Red Sea, into the Bab al Mandeb. Traffic has been pretty significantly diverted away from the Strait of Hormuz towards this other maritime choke point. But that maritime choke point also is where Yemen is located and where the Houthis, are located.

“And so if you're Iran, and you understand that, you know, the Americans are trying to take away your trump card in terms of leverage, what you'll be looking for is additional leverage. So I actually expect the Houthis to become a bigger problem potentially in the future that are going to require a more resolute response than we've seen up until this point.”

News.title: Pope Leo addresses 'the rich and powerful' in new message as Trump feud rages on
News.content:
Pope Leo addresses 'the rich and powerful' in new message as Trump feud rages on

Pope Leo addressed the 'rich and powerful' in a new message today as the Vatican's feud with Donald Trump and JD Vance over the Iran war continues

View 3 Images Pope Leo is currently touring Africa (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Pope Leo addressed the need to resist "the whims of the rich and powerful" today after being criticised by Donald Trump.

‌



The Pope, who is currently touring Africa, urged Cameroon's government to resist the super wealthy while speaking in front of President Paul Biya.

‌



"It is time to examine our conscience and take a bold leap forward," he told Biya, Prime Minister Joseph Dion Ngute and other leaders. "In order for peace and justice to prevail, the chains of corruption - which disfigure authority and strip it of its credibility - must be broken," he said.

‌



"Hearts must be set free from an idolatrous thirst for profit." He also called for an end to the Anglophone war in Cameroon, in which thousands of people have been killed.

View 3 Images Trump has been critical of the Pope (Image: Getty Images)

It comes amid a growing back and forth between the Pope and Trump, with the US president attacking the pontiff over his criticism of the Iran war, and the Pope responding that he has "no fear" of the Trump administration.

‌



On Sunday, Trump slammed the Pope as "weak on crime and terrible for foreign policy" before telling reporters: "I'm not a fan of Pope Leo."

"Pope Leo is WEAK on Crime, and terrible for Foreign Policy," the president wrote in a scathing Truth Social post, adding: "I don't want a Pope who thinks it's OK for Iran to have a Nuclear Weapon."

Yesterday, the Pope issued a message on X addressing "the arrogant". He said: "God's heart is torn apart by wars, violence, injustice and lies. But our Father's heart is not with the wicked, the arrogant, or the proud. God's heart is with the little ones and the humble, and with them He builds up His Kingdom of love and peace day by day. Wherever there is love and service, God is there."

‌



View 3 Images Vance pushed back on the Pope's comments too

Later, JD Vance pushed back on Pope Leo's claim that God is never on the side of those who wage a war, saying there is a "more than 1,000 year tradition of just war theory".

Speaking at a Turning Point USA event at the University of Georgia yesterday, Vance added: "We can, of course, have disagreements about whether this or that conflict is just."

Article continues below

The Vatican has since responded to Vance. The Vatican's editorial director, Andrea Tornielli, said "just war" theory was developed centuries ago, when wars were fought with swords - not machine-guided drones.

He said: "Reflections based on the theology of past centuries and possible justifications for war fail to take into account that when theologians of earlier times wrote about these issues, wars were fought with swords and clubs - not with deadly weapons and machine-guided drones, a reality that raises moral questions of dramatic intensity. There has been a growing awareness that war is not a path to be followed."

News.title: Keir Starmer hits back as ex-Nato boss warns British security 'in peril'
News.content:
Keir Starmer hits back as ex-Nato boss warns British security 'in peril'

Lord Robertson, a former Labour defence secretary who co-authored last year's Strategic Defence Review, issued a stark warning about Britain's military security

View 2 Images Keir Starmer has been accused of complacency over defence (Image: House of Commons/PA Wire)

Keir Starmer has rejected a scathing public attack by a former Nato chief, who accused the Government of a “corrosive complacency” on defence.

‌



The Prime Minister is under pressure to publish a long-delayed defence investment plan amid questions about Britain’s military capabilities in a more turbulent world. In an explosive intervention, Lord Robertson, a former Labour defence secretary who co-authored last year's Strategic Defence Review, warned the UK’s security was “in peril” and accused the Treasury of “vandalism”.

‌



However Mr Starmer told MPs: “I respect Lord Robertson and I thank him again for carrying out the strategic (defence) review. My responsibility is to keep the British people safe, and that is a duty I take seriously. That is why I don’t agree with his comments.”

‌



The PM insisted defence spending was rising rapidly and said Labour had inherited "uncosted and undeliverable" plans from the Tories. He pointed to the decision last year to hike defence spending to 2.5% of GDP, funded by cuts to the foreign aid budget, and further commitments to raise core defence spending to 3.5% by 2035, in line with a new Nato target.

OPINION Mikey Smith Donald Trump's most unhinged 48 hours as president in 11 bizarre moments

View 2 Images Concerns have been raised over the state of Britain's defence

‌



It comes after reports Rachel Reeves is looking to put up spending by £10billion over four years, despite military chiefs warning of a £28bn shortfall after years of underinvestment. The 10-year defence investment plan was due to be published in the autumn but has still not been signed off as negotiations with the Treasury run on.

Lord Robertson went public with his criticism this week, blaming the rising welfare budget and a lack of urgency from the PM for the UK being unprepared for war. He said: “We cannot defend Britain with an ever-expanding welfare budget.”

Defence Secretary John Healey also said he did not agree with Lord Robertson’s assessment. Speaking after a meeting of the Ukraine Defence Contact Group, Mr Healey said: “There’s no complacency, and we are getting on with the job in Government, we’re getting on with the job of delivering that strategic defence review, of defending Britain.”

‌



The Defence Secretary went on: "I would say to our politicians in parliament as I say to the British public: we know the threats that we face in Britain and that we face together as NATO allies are rising.

"We know the demands on defence are rising. We have demonstrated in less than two years as a Labour government that we are ready to make the decisions to increase defence investment, and we are doing that by the biggest amount since the end of the Cold War."

But Labour MP Tan Dhesi, who chairs the defence select committee, said the warning was sobering. He told the Commons: "His comments align with what the Defence Committee has been highlighting for several months now, that we are ill prepared to face the threats that we as a nation currently are facing in a more volatile world.

Article continues below

"And that is why the Government's rhetoric must align with reality, and we must ensure that we get to that 3% GDP spend on defence in this Parliament. "We cannot afford to kick the can down the road to the next Parliament."

Emma Lewell, the Labour MP for South Shields, said bolstering defence investment “should not come at the expense of those pensioners and people with disabilities receiving welfare”.

News.title: Southport killer so dangerous FOUR prison officers guard him when he leaves cell
News.content:
Southport killer so dangerous FOUR prison officers guard him when he leaves cell

Prison guards are allegedly 'terrified' of Southport killer Axel Rudakubana and have put strict rules on the killer while at a notorious jail HMP Belmarsh in London

View 4 Images Court sketch of Axel Rudakubana (Image: PA)

The evil Southport child murderer has led to prison security being increased - with four guards reportedly following him outside of his cell.

‌



Axel Rudakubana, 19, is serving life with a minimum of 52 years behind bars for murder of three young girls at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class. The killer is being held at the notorious HMP Belmarsh, in South East London, where he allegedly previously threw boiling water on prison officers.

‌



Rudakubana is reportedly being kept on a "safe systems" which means he can only leave his cell and move around the jail while being escorted by at least four prison guards.

‌



View 4 Images Alice da Silva Aguiar was killed in Southport (Image: PA)

Southport Inquiry lists 67 key recommendations — see full list of themes READ MORE :

Signs Southport attacker would kill - from knives and disturbing searches to Childline call READ MORE :

A damning inquiry said the horror 2024 stabbing, which shocked the UK, could have been prevented. The report said it was "highly likely" the crime would not have happened if various agencies dealt with the teen's behaviour.

The report also concluded if Rudakubana's parents "had done what they morally ought to have done" then he "would not have been at liberty to conduct the attack and it would not therefore have occurred".

‌



A source, according to The Sun, claimed guards were scared of the child killer, saying: "They are taking no chances with him due to the inquiry and his history of violence. Prison officers are frightened of him and rightly so. They fear he could make a weapon or try another attack like the one he carried out.

"He is deemed a massive danger so they will only unlock his door when they are mob-handed to make sure they can control him if he tries anything. At least one of the officers will have a body-worn camera every time they interact with him as well."

4 View 4 Images Bebe King was six when she died (Image: PA) 4 View 4 Images Elsie Dot Stancombe (Image: PA)

‌



The source also claimed the 19-year-old and his behaviour has not changed "despite all the sessions with psychologists and therapists" and officers think he is "likely to commit further attacks in jail".

It was also claimed a lack of resources has meant the child killer is kept in his cell for "23 hours per day a lot of the time" due to the number of people that need to escort him around Belmarsh. The Mirror has reached out to the Ministry of Justice for comment.

Rudakubana, in May, 2025, allegedly attacked two officers in prison with boiling water from a kettle. They were rushed to hospital and discharged on the same day. At the time, the Ministry of Justice said it was investigating the incident.

Article continues below

This comes after the parents of the three girls killed in the Southport attack said the killer's parents have "blood on their hands", their solicitor said after the inquiry.

Bebe King, six, Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, were killed in the July 29, 2024, attack. Chris Walker, from law firm Bond Turner, said: "We call for disciplinary proceedings to ensue against those individuals, who I know the names of. We want disciplinary proceedings against them to begin and to finish swiftly and that includes people losing their jobs.

"If we are not satisfied with the outcome of those disciplinary proceedings from a managerial level to a lower, coalface, level, to use that expression, then I will be publicly naming those individuals as people we say are not fit to serve in a public office."

News.title: King Charles's visit to the US comes at crucial time in 'special relationship' history
News.content:
King Charles's visit to the US comes at crucial time in 'special relationship' history

As President Trump ramps up threats to Britain for not joining his war in Iran, King Charles has a chance to show the power of soft diplomacy in action with his visit to the US

View 3 Images President Trump has referred to King Charles as his "good friend" in the past (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

With the so-called ‘special relationship’ in the balance and Britain under threat of being cut off by the United States, the stakes could not be higher.

‌



The King’s visit to America comes at a time when the wrath of President Trump for failing to support his illegal war with Iran grows with each day that passes.

‌



His very public displeasure with our Prime Minister, among other world leaders who have not bowed to his demands, has created an ugly war of words and menaces from this bully President.

‌



Yet, for Starmer’s “tragic mistake” in not backing Trump’s badly thought out attacks on Iran, the President has continued to heap praise on “great gentleman” and “friend of mine” King Charles.

This is a time when the soft-power diplomacy of the royal family is needed more than ever.

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s Australia tour IS being funded in part by taxpayers READ MORE :

View 3 Images President Trump has referred to King Charles as his "good friend" in the past (Image: AP)

‌



Following Trump’s unprecedented second State Visit to the UK last September, the President has been keen to return the honour to a man - and institution - he genuinely holds in high regard.

No wonder the British government is keen to send our King and Queen into the fray.

The trip has taken six months to plan, with Buckingham Palace and the White House fully across the minute details of engagements, handshakes and key moments likely to be recognised by the world’s media.

‌



Notably, however, there will be no Oval Office public meeting for the King - no doubt after the embarrassing exchanges between Trump and a succession of world leaders, including Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky in recent months.

View 3 Images The British government will be hoping King Charles can wield the soft power needed to maintain the 'special relationship' (Image: PA)

Instead, Charles and Queen Camilla will have a private tea with the US President and wife Melania soon after their arrival on April 27.

‌



The King and Mr Trump will then have a meeting without media present the next day at the White House.

While royal sources have admitted there is at least a degree of expectation that Trump will veer off script, those at the top do not believe the President would dare to embarrass the King and Queen given the “genuine warmth” between them.

While Charles and The Donald may hugely disagree on most things - the environment, respect for the Pope and peace in the Middle East, to name a few - the King may just be the calming influence that is needed.

Article continues below

As the threats to the UK and Keir Starmer continue, including the warning that the recently signed trade deal could be torn up over disagreements in his Middle East policy, the royals have a huge task ahead.

News.title: Police say Epsom rape suspects unknown as crowds and cops with shields gather
News.content:
Police say Epsom rape suspects unknown as crowds and cops with shields gather

Police are working to identify suspects after a woman was raped outside Epsom Methodist Church in Surrey on Saturday - crowds gathered in the town on Wednesday afternoon

View 3 Images Police in riot gear stood by as crowds gathered in Epsom on Wednesday afternoon (Image: UKSploosh/Youtube)

Police are yet to identify a group of men who raped a woman outside a church in a Surrey town.

‌



The woman in her 20s was followed by several men after leaving Labyrinth Epsom nightclub and attacked outside Epsom Methodist Church on Ashley Road between 2am and 4am on Saturday, Surrey Police said. In an update on Wednesday, the force said it has interviewed a number of witnesses, carried out house-to-house enquiries and is reviewing CCTV footage.

‌



Videos shared on social media on Wednesday afternoon showed crowds gathering in Epsom, while police vehicles and officers in riot gear, including shields, stood across from them on the other side of the street.

‌



Surrey Police said: "Unfortunately at this stage, we still do not have sufficient information to release the descriptions of the suspects. However, we are continuing to work with the victim, who is being supported by a specialist Sexual Offences Liaison Officer through the process, to progress these enquiries."

View 3 Images A woman was allegedly raped by several men near Epsom Methodist Church (Image: Google Maps)

East Surrey Chief Superintendent Mark Chapman said: "I understand the distress and concern that this incident has caused, both for the victim herself and amongst our local communities, and I want you to reassure you that we are working hard to progress this investigation.

‌



"While we have already carried out extensive enquiries, we do not have sufficient information at this time to update you with the descriptions of the suspects."

He added: "In the meantime, I would urge people not to speculate about the descriptions of these suspects as this may lead to additional tensions within our local communities. I would also like to reassure you that we have stepped up patrols in the area, and this increased police presence will continue over the weekend."

View 3 Images People gathered in Epsom on Wednesday afternoon (Image: UKSploosh/Youtube)

‌



Epsom MP Helen Maguire said the attack had "understandably caused real distress" in the town, adding: "My heart goes out to the young woman at the centre of this deeply distressing incident."

"The most important thing is that Surrey Police can carry out their investigation thoroughly, and without interference," she said, urging the public to "refrain from speculation, particularly online".

Ch Supt Chapman urged anyone with information to contact police, quoting reference PR/45260041426 or using the force's online form.

Article continues below

Officers are particularly keen to speak to anyone who was in the area around Ashley Road, Epsom Methodist Church or Labyrinth Epsom nightclub between 2am and 4am on Saturday, or who saw or spoke to a woman in her 20s who appeared to be in distress.

Anyone with CCTV, dashcam or helmet cam footage from the area during that time is also asked to come forward.

Murray will be remembered for his razor-sharp volleying skills and the preposterous angles he conjured at the net. His returns were often unorthodox and he was fond of a lobbed service return to unsettle opponents.

Alongside his triumphs, Murray has been a staunch defender of doubles players and frequently demanded they be shown more respect.

Hugo Ekitike has been ruled out of the World Cup after suffering a ruptured Achilles tendon in Liverpool’s Champions League exit to Paris Saint-Germain.

Ekitike was stretchered off half an hour into the contest after going down off the ball and France manager Didier Deschamps has now confirmed in a statement that the striker will be absent for this summer’s tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico, with his season with Liverpool over.

"Hugo suffered a serious injury on Tuesday evening against PSG. The severity of his injury will unfortunately prevent him from finishing the season with Liverpool and participating in the World Cup,” Deschamps said.

Liverpool manager Arne Slot admitted after the quarter-final clash, which the Reds lost 4-0 on aggregate, that the injury looked “really bad”, while defender Ibrahima Konate - Ekitike’s teammate for both club and country - said that “because with the World Cup coming it is very, very hard for him and I send him my prayers”.

The 23-year-old has eight caps for France after breaking into the squad last September and was set to be selected by Deschamps as one of his forward options.

He has scored two goals for his country, including one in the 2-1 friendly win over Brazil during the March international break, which took place at the Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts - a World Cup venue for this summer.

“Hugo is one of the dozen young players who have made their debuts with the national team in recent months. He had perfectly integrated into the group, both on the pitch and off it,” Deschamps added.

open image in gallery Liverpool forward Hugo Ekitike is carried off on a stretcher against PSG (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Wire )

“This injury is a huge blow for him, of course, but also for the France team. His disappointment is immense.

“Hugo will regain his top form, I'm convinced of it. But I wanted to express all my support to him, as well as that of the entire staff. We know he'll be fully behind the France team, and we're all thinking of him very strongly."

France are drawn in Group I for the World Cup and will start their campaign against Senegal on 16 June at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium - where the World Cup final will be held - before facing Iraq on 22 June and Norway on 26 June.

Congress is set to take up the reauthorization of a divisive program that lets U.S. spy agencies pore over foreigners' calls, texts and emails.

President Donald Trump has been urging lawmakers to extend FISA 702, saying it is “desperately needed,” while critics point to long-standing concerns about warrantless surveillance of Americans.

A key provision of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act permits the CIA, National Security Agency, FBI and other agencies to collect and analyze vast amounts of overseas communications without a warrant. It incidentally sweeps up the conversations of any Americans who interact with those foreigners targeted for surveillance.

The program expires Monday, and critics want changes, including a requirement for warrants before authorities can access the emails, phone calls or text messages of Americans.

They also want limits on the government's use of internet data brokers, who sell large volumes of personal information gleaned online, offering the government what critics say amounts to an end-run around the Constitution.

President Trump has urged lawmakers to extend the foreign surveillance program for 18 more months ( AFP via Getty Images )

House Republican leaders hoped to advance the legislation on Wednesday, but an initial procedural step was delayed. Rank-and-file members have pushed back despite a pressure campaign that included a trip to the White House and direct involvement from CIA Director John Ratcliffe.

The chances of significant changes, however, seem have dropped since Trump announced his support for the program's renewal, saying it had proved its worth in supplying information vital to recent U.S. actions in Venezuela and Iran.

“The fact is, whether you like FISA or not, it is extremely important to our military,” Trump said on social media Tuesday.

Trump calls for another extension of the program

U.S. authorities say the program, known as Section 702 of the law, is essential to national security and has saved lives by uncovering terrorist plots. Critics question what they say is a dangerous infringement on civil liberties and privacy.

In a Truth Social post, Trump said a different FISA provision was used to spy on his 2016 campaign but that he supported Section 702's renewal despite misgivings that political adversaries could use parts of the law against him in the future. He urged lawmakers to extend the foreign surveillance program for 18 more months.

“My administration has worked tirelessly to ensure these FISA reforms are being aggressively executed at every level of the Executive Branch to keep Americans safe, while protecting our sacred Civil Liberties guaranteed by our Great Constitution,” Trump wrote.

The Republican president is a longtime critic of the nation's intelligence services and was once opposed to Section 702 before he reversed himself. His director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, sponsored legislation to repeal Section 702 as a Hawaii congresswoman but now supports it. She says new protections added since her time in Congress helped change her mind.

Some Republican House members who have opposed the extension without changes went to the White House late Tuesday to discuss the matter. Ratcliffe also met with lawmakers early Wednesday.

“I am asking Republicans to UNIFY, and vote together on the test vote to bring a clean Bill to the floor,” Trump said Wednesday. “We need to stick together.”

Greater protections are sought for Americans' communications

In addition to a requirement for a warrant to access Americans' data, critics also want greater protections on how the FBI or other agencies can search communications and how that is reported to the public.

“Journalists, foreign aid workers, people with family overseas, all could have their communications swept up in this surveillance merely because they talked to someone outside of this country,” said Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore. He is pushing for changes that he said will ensure the government is not violating civil rights in secret.

Several Republicans also have suggested changes, such as the warrant requirement.

“National security and civil liberties are not mutually exclusive,” said Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz. “We can give our intelligence professionals the tools they need to target foreign threats while ensuring that Americans are not subjected to unconstitutional surveillance.”

Gabbard's office releases an annual report showing the number of foreign surveillance targets and number of searches likely to identify an American. For 2025, the number of foreign surveillance targets increased to nearly 350,000 from almost 292,000 in 2024. Searches using terms likely to identify an American decreased slightly to 7,724 from 7,845 in 2024.

The totals are incomplete because agencies such as the FBI have found ways to access the data without reporting the searches publicly, said Elizabeth Goitein, senior director of the Liberty and National Security Program at the Brennan Center for Justice at New York University.

FBI officials repeatedly violated their own standards when searching for intelligence related to the Jan. 6, 2021, riot at the Capitol and racial justice protests in 2020, according to a 2024 court order.

“It’s reminiscent of J. Edgar Hoover's tenure at the FBI,” Goitein said, referring to the FBI's founding director who used illegal surveillance to harass and spy on Americans. “They can pretty much target anyone."

There's little time to make changes to the law

Despite bipartisan concerns about the law and its implications for civil liberties, time is running out for Congress to make any changes before Monday's expiration.

Trump's support also reduces the odds that enough Republicans will break ranks and join Democrats to push for an overhaul.

Rep. Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, announced a proposal Tuesday that would require the Justice Department to seek a court order before the FBI could access search results involving Americans. Himes said in a statement that he wants to see Section 702 renewed with new protections.

It “is too critical to allow it to expire, but the legitimate concerns about the possibility of abuse also demand that we consider additional reforms,” he said.

The best chance for inserting changes likely is the House, where a large number of lawmakers from both parties have expressed concerns.

But Rep. Rick Crawford, an Arkansas Republican who leads the House Intelligence Committee, is backing Trump's call for an 18-month renewal.

Crawford has said he believes the government can empower spy agencies while also holding them accountable.

The NBA has declared its new television deals a resounding success after reporting record viewership figures for the past season.

The league announced on Wednesday that 170 million people in the United States tuned into NBA games across its four primary broadcast platforms – ABC/ESPN, Amazon Prime Video, NBC/Peacock, and NBA TV.

These figures mark the league's highest viewership in 24 years, representing an 86 per cent increase on last season.

This season marked the debut of Prime Video as part of the league's television rights package, while NBC/Peacock returned for the first time in a generation.

These platforms are part of a new 11-year media rights deal, valued at over $76 billion, signed in 2024, which commenced at the start of the current season.

open image in gallery NBA viewing figures have risen to a 24-year high ( Reuters )

Further highlights from the viewership data include the highest average viewership in 13 years, a 35 per cent rise from last season.

Fifty-seven telecasts this season attracted an average of two million viewers, the most since the 2011-12 season.

Furthermore, fans collectively watched NBA games for more than 920 million hours, a 25 per cent increase on last season and the highest total since 2011-12.

The NBA's social media platforms also saw record engagement, generating 228 billion views this season, according to Videocites, an increase of 13 per cent.

Arena attendance over the last three seasons has surpassed any comparable period in the league's history.

Viewership for NBA Cup group stage matches surged by 90 per cent, and the All-Star Game, broadcast on NBC, drew an audience of 8.8 million, making it the most-watched mid-season showcase since 2011.

The SoFI NBA Play-In Tournament began on Tuesday and is due to run until Friday.

The NBA playoffs will then start on Saturday, while the 2026 NBA Draft Lottery is scheduled for 10 May.

Children as young as 13 could be recommended sexually explicit content on Elon Musk’s X, according to a new report exposing potential breaches of the Online Safety Act.

The Centre of Countering Digital Hate warned that X’s algorithm and “weak safeguards” recommended pornography to teenagers and exposed them to possible direct sexual contact from adults.

Researchers from the non-profit organisation set up two accounts based in the UK, pretending to be a 13-year-old boy and girl, in order to test X’s adult content policy through its search results, algorithm, profiles and Communities section.

To test the search bar, researchers entered sexual terms that “a curious teenager might naturally search for”, such as “sex, porn, boobs, and hentai”, the report said, and found that 80 per cent of searches for sexual terms returned some explicit results, with that content appearing within the first ten results that contained media.

open image in gallery Teen accounts were able to join 15 out of 20 popular sexual communities on X ( CCDH )

Multiple videos and images came up of women performing oral sex on a man, as well as a video of a woman lying on a sofa masturbating. No age verification, content warning, or filtering step intervened between the teen account and any explicit material brought up in the search bar.

The researchers found that after these explicit searches, the account’s For You algorithm was altered to include graphic images; 30.5 per cent of recommended posts in the feed were explicit.

These accounts were also able to join 15 out of 20 adult sexual communities with ease, including groups named “Virgin Trades”, “Onlyfans virgin club +18”, “Kink Kings & Queens” and “Goon Group”. These communities had overtly sexual and transactional content, including posts soliciting or offering nude images, according to the report.

To test whether community participation would lead to direct contact between adults and teenagers, researchers liked posts in the community where users offered to send messages for engagement.

open image in gallery Elon Musk acquired X, then known as Twitter, in 2022 ( AFP/Getty )

The teen accounts were able to bypass default settings that mean they can only receive direct messages from accounts they follow, an attempt to safeguard them. In doing this, the accounts received numerous direct message requests from adult accounts, including one unsolicited video of a man masturbating.

It comes almost a year after the Online Safety Act, which has legislated tech platforms must enforce age limits to protect child users from harmful content. Adult sites, including the world’s most visited, PornHub, have been forced to introduce age verification for UK visitors as part of the government crackdown.

Services that don’t comply could face fines of 10 per cent of worldwide annual revenues or £18 million, whichever is greater.

Ofcom opened an investigation earlier this year into reports of its Grok AI chatbot being used to create and share sexual deepfakes of real people, including children.

X has since claimed it implemented measures to try and address the issue, although a report by NBC News on Tuesday suggested the AI chatbot was still generating dozens of sexual images and videos depicting real people.

open image in gallery Ofcom opened investigations and into X and Grok earlier this year ( Reuters )

The Children’s Commissioner for England issued a warning last August that X “remains the most common source of pornography for children, outstripping even dedicated pornography sites.”

Callum Hood, head of research at CCDH UK said the findings were proof that X needed to take its responsibility to protect children more seriously: “These findings show X will quickly reshape its ‘For You’ feed to recommend explicit content to young users. Worse, with a single change to account settings, adults can directly message them, leaving children exposed to more explicit sexual material and the risk of grooming.

“Nearly a year after enforcement began, X is still failing to comply with the Online Safety Act, allowing children into sexualised spaces and continuing to host harmful content. How much more evidence is needed before X takes its responsibility to protect children seriously?”

open image in gallery Platforms such as Pornhub have had to include age verification since the Online Safety Act ( AFP/Getty )

He warned that this increased the risk of grooming and sexual exploitation for children.

“The risk is not just that explicit content exists, it is how quickly and consistently it is recommended to young users. A child can make a simple search and be shown graphic sexual material within seconds, which is then repeatedly recommended in their feed,” he explained. “That creates a pathway that goes from simple curiosity to ongoing exposure, and even into spaces where adults could contact them. This significantly increases the risk of grooming and exploitation.”

An Ofcom spokesperson said: “Protecting children is a priority for Ofcom. Under the Online Safety Act, tech firms are accountable for ensuring sites, platforms and apps are safer for the children who use them. They must take a safety-first approach in how their services are designed and operated, including by combatting grooming, tackling child sexual abuse material, and using age checks to prevent kids from accessing pornography.

“Those companies that do not comply can expect to face enforcement action. We’ve launched investigations into more than 100 platforms, including X, and issued over a dozen fines for non-compliance.”

A Department for Science, Innovation and Technology spokesperson said: “These findings are disturbing. Platforms have a clear responsibility under the Act to protect children from harmful content. They must step up and take responsibility.

“Ofcom has strong enforcement powers it can use where platforms fail to comply with the law and has already issued over £3 million in fines. They have our full backing to act where necessary.

“We have also launched a consultation on the next steps to give kids the childhood they deserve. We are looking at everything from age limits and safer design features on AI chatbots and games, to a social media ban."

The Independent has approached X for comment.

Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel blasted Vice President JD Vance for defending Donald Trump after the president posted an AI-generated image online which portrayed him as Jesus.

Trump shared the image on Truth Social Sunday after dubbing Pope Leo XIV as “WEAK” on crime, following the pontiff’s criticism of the U.S. war with Iran. The AI image showed Trump wearing robes and healing a sick man with beams of light coming from his hands.

The post received fierce backlash from Christians and political figures on both sides of the aisle. Trump took the image down Monday, claiming that he thought it had portrayed him as a doctor, not Jesus.

Vance, who converted to Catholicism in 2019, subsequently claimed the image was “a joke” during an interview with Fox News’ Bret BaierMonday. ​But Kimmel was having none of the excuses.

“Trump is doing his best to upset every faction of Christianity,” the Jimmy Kimmel Live! host said Tuesday. “After he lambasted the pope, he posted an image of himself as Jesus, and then when everyone got mad, he said, ‘Oh I didn’t know that was Jesus, I thought that was me as a doctor healing people,’ which is so lame. Not one person believes it. It is quite clearly an image of Jesus with his dumb head on it.”

open image in gallery Kimmel said ‘not one person’ believes Trump’s excuse for sharing an image that portrayed the president as Jesus ( Jimmy Kimmel Live! )

open image in gallery The post received fierce backlash from Christians and political figures on both sides of the aisle. Trump took the image down Monday, claiming that he thought it had portrayed him as a doctor, not Jesus ( @realDonaldTrump/Truth Social )

Kimmel noted that not even Vance was “able to go along with this doctor storyline,” and was forced to come up with an entirely different narrative.

The late-night host then played a clip of Vance on Fox News.

“I think the president was posting a joke, and of course he took it down because he recognized that a lot of people weren’t understanding his humor in that case,” the vice president claimed.

Kimmel then said: “He was posting a joke, you understand? And like all the best jokes, it had to be explained and then deleted. First, he was Jesus. Then he wasn’t Jesus, he was a doctor. And now, it was a joke.”

He added: “Why did I get kicked off the air again? I can’t remember.”

Kimmel’s show was suspended in September over comments he made about the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, who was shot and killed during a live debate on a Utah college campus.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump claimed he thought the image he shared online depicted him as a doctor, not Jesus ( Getty )

During the show, Kimmel said that the MAGA world was “desperately trying to characterize this kid who murdered Charlie Kirk as anything other than one of them, and doing everything they can to score political points from it.”

ABC brought Jimmy Kimmel Live! back on air the following week.

Meanwhile, Trump seems unfazed by the Jesus image furor. On Wednesday, the president shared another image on Truth Social that showed Jesus giving him a hug.

The new image, which appeared to be AI-generated, shows Jesus with an arm around Trump’s shoulder and one hand on his chest. The two are standing in front of a halo of light and an American flag, and have their heads leaning against each other.

Trump captioned the image: “The Radical Left Lunatics might not like this, but I think it is quite nice!!! President DJT.”
